records.description: The hydrogen ecosystem has developed substantially over the past decade, yet investment volatility and other challenges will require a reinvigorated and cohesive effort to enable success, writes Sunita Satyapal.

records.title: An evolving research agenda for the transition to electrified transport
records.description: Transport electrification is reshaping energy and mobility systems while posing infrastructure, supply chain, and societal challenges that demand bold, interconnected research, argues Patrick Plötz.

records.title: Levers to address energy insecurity in the United States
records.description: A wide range of policies and actions can be used to address energy insecurity, and there are many actors and institutions to carry them out. This Perspective provides an overview of the many levers, or opportunities, that electricity sector actors have to reduce energy insecurity and affordability in the United States.

records.title: Aqueous eutectic electrolytes suppress oxygen and hydrogen evolution for long-life Zn||MnO 2 dual-electrode-free batteries
records.description: Eutectic aqueous–organic electrolytes enable highly reversible zinc–manganese batteries without acid addition. By regulating the water-bonding network, beneficial manganese oxide phases are deposited and stripped while gas formation is suppressed, achieving ultraextended cycling.

records.title: Molecularly aligned electron channels for ultrafast-charging practical lithium-metal batteries
records.description: Sluggish interfacial charge transfer in Li-metal batteries limits ultrafast charging and causes side reactions. The authors design solvent molecules to enhance Li⁺ coordination, improving the charge-transfer kinetics and enabling stable high-rate cycling of Li-metal cells.

records.title: Managing the geopolitics of Europe’s fossil-fuel exit
records.description: As Europe gradually phases out its fossil-fuel imports, some producer economies face rising risks. With careful management, the European Union can turn this shift into an opportunity to advance both climate leadership and geopolitical stability.

records.title: Atomistic origins of anharmonic lattice dynamics and thermal expansion in perovskite photovoltaics
records.description: Metal halide perovskites exhibit anharmonic lattice vibrations, which lead to high rates of thermal expansion in solar cells. In this Review, Julian A. Steele links the atomistic origins of these effects to the macroscopic thermo-mechanical properties of the materials and devices.

records.title: Harnessing interfacial solvation structure for next-generation secondary batteries
records.description: Ion–solvent interactions at battery interfaces share parallels with solvation effects in catalysis. This analysis examines how interfacial solvation structures influence interphase formation and charge transfer, offering insights into electrochemical behaviour under complex conditions.

records.title: Lessons from copper indium gallium sulfo-selenide solar cells for progressing perovskite photovoltaics
records.description: Perovskite photovoltaics could benefit from insights gained through the longer history of other photovoltaic technologies. In this Perspective, Bermudez and colleagues examine how lessons from the successes and failures of copper indium gallium selenide solar cells can guide future progress.

records.title: Behavioural choices shape US indoor temperatures more than technology
records.description: Households that manually manage thermostats keep homes warmer in winter and cooler in summer than those using automated smart thermostat features, leading to increased energy use and costs. Expanding equitable access to smart thermostats and supporting behavioural engagement could improve indoor thermal comfort, reduce energy costs, and narrow disparities in thermal safety.

records.title: The role of thermostats and human behaviour in residential temperature settings in the USA
records.description: Smart thermostats and programmed temperature settings support more efficient heating and cooling. New research finds that renters, low-income and Black households are less likely to have this technology in the USA.

records.title: Regulation of hydrothermal kinetics unlocks record efficiency in Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cells
records.description: Regulating hydrothermal reaction kinetics using sodium sulfide achieves a flattened valence band maximum across the Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 film, lifting the potential barrier for hole transport while suppressing deep-level defect formation and reducing trap centres. This strategy enables Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cells to reach a certified record efficiency of 10.7%.

records.title: Regulation of hydrothermal reaction kinetics with sodium sulfide for certified 10.7% efficiency Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cells
records.description: Controlling the hydrothermal reaction kinetics during the fabrication of Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cells is challenging. Chen Qian et al. show that sodium sulfide buffers the pH and allows a controlled release of Se, enabling a certified efficiency of 10.7%.

records.title: Co-crystal engineering unlocks high-stability perovskite solar modules
records.description: Instability hinders the commercialization of perovskite solar cells. Now, a co-crystal engineering strategy is developed to create a protective two-dimensional perovskite layer on top of a three-dimensional perovskite layer. This approach increases the stability and efficiency of perovskite solar modules, surpassing current photovoltaic standards, in a step towards industrial manufacturing.

records.title: Battery-electric passenger vehicles will be cost-effective across Africa well before 2040
records.description: Decarbonizing road transport is critical, but the costs and emissions of low-carbon vehicles in Africa remain uncertain. The authors show that battery electric vehicles with solar off-grid systems can cost effectively reduce life-cycle emissions well before 2040.

records.title: Mapping Europe’s rooftop photovoltaic potential with a building-level database
records.description: This resource presents an open per-building dataset of rooftop solar photovoltaics potential for the European Union. The results show that potential capacity could cover approximately 40% of electricity demand in a 100% renewable scenario for 2050.

records.title: Formation pathway of high-efficiency kesterite solar cells fabricated through molecular ink chemistry
records.description: Photovoltaics based on kesterite materials have now achieved 15% efficiency after remaining at lower levels for years. In this Review, Jimenez-Arguijo et al. explore the critical roles of precursor chemistry and the formation pathway in enabling performance improvements in these complex multinary semiconductors.

records.title: A just energy transition requires just-shoring critical materials
Selenium hits double digits
records.description: Of the many families of solar absorber materials known, only a handful have been shown to convert sunlight into electricity with power conversion efficiencies above 10%. Now, researchers have pushed selenium photovoltaics past this efficiency threshold by implementing a series of improvements to the material processing and device design.

records.title: Illumination-assisted annealing enables selenium solar cells with open-circuit voltage over 1 V and efficiency exceeding 10%
records.description: The efficiency of selenium photovoltaics is hindered by the poor crystallization of the Se film. Wen, Li, Lu and colleagues use light to initiate Se crystallization, suppressing dewetting and enabling the formation of a continuous film, which achieves a certified efficiency of 10.3%.

records.title: Fuel poverty risk at the end of life needs urgent attention
records.description: Proactive policy and economic support are needed to reduce fuel poverty risk at the end of life, argues Elaine Robinson.

records.title: Amorphous grain boundary engineering for scalable flexible perovskite photovoltaics with improved stability
records.description: The mechanical reliability and scalability of flexible perovskite solar cells remain challenging. Mingzhu He et al. design β-cyclodextrin derivatives to reinforce grain boundaries, enhancing both the efficiency and stability of cells and modules.

records.title: Negative pricing increases electricity use but challenges grid stability
records.description: When electricity supply exceeds demand, consumers can be paid to use electricity through negative pricing. Simulations based on national surveys indicate that such pricing could double electricity loads in many US counties. However, market policies and grids must be carefully designed to avoid destabilizing the power grid with demand surges.

records.title: Approaching the theoretical density limit of ultrahigh-nickel cathodes via cation-disorder-free 10-μm single-crystalline particles
records.description: Single-crystalline layered oxides can reduce capacity decay in nickel-rich cathodes, but controlling both the particle size and cation disorder is challenging. This work reports cation-disorder-free ~10-μm single-crystalline cathodes that deliver high volumetric capacity and cycle stability as well as improved safety.

records.title: Author Correction: Dynamic cycling enhances battery lifetime
An organic semiconductor-based photocatalyst sheet for overall solar-driven water splitting
records.description: Solar water splitting offers a route to renewable hydrogen, but developing photocatalyst sheets from scalable, solution-processable materials remains a challenge. Here the authors use underlayer engineering to build an organic semiconductor photocatalyst sheet that enables unassisted overall water splitting under simulated sunlight.

records.title: Author Correction: Heat treatment in an oxygen-rich environment to suppress deep-level traps in Cu 2 ZnSnS 4 solar cell with 11.51% certified efficiency
Data centres asymmetrically exacerbate energy burdens through wholesale price increases and regressive grid cost shifting
records.description: As data centres increase pressure on power systems, the costs of accommodating their growth are becoming a concern. Here the researchers show that data centres raise wholesale prices and shift transmission costs onto households, with the largest burden increases in rural and low-income communities.

records.title: Author Correction: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics
Directing solvent reactivity
records.description: Anode-free sodium batteries eliminate excessive sodium on the anode, maximizing cell-level energy density, but are limited by irreversible sodium loss during electroplating–stripping. Now, a low-strain cyclic solvent forms an oligomerized interphase, enabling highly reversible sodium deposition without functional additives or electrode modifications.

records.title: Stable anode-free sodium batteries enabled by controlled oligomerization
records.description: Anode-free sodium batteries are limited by irreversible sodium loss during cycling. Here the authors introduce a moderate-strain cyclic ether that redirects electrolyte decomposition to form a thin, robust interphase, thereby minimizing sodium consumption and extending cycling stability.

records.title: Grain boundary engineering using metallomesogen in formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide for stable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells
records.description: Formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide perovskites show promise in terms of stability, yet their solar cell efficiency remains limited. Li et al. use a metallomesogen with mesophase to stabilize perovskite grain boundaries, improving both the efficiency and stability of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells.

records.title: Ironing out oxygen instability
records.description: Oxygen redox in layered-oxide cathodes could facilitate the development of high-energy sodium-ion batteries, but poor reversibility has limited its practical application. Now, an iron-mediated redox strategy offers a pathway to substantially improving oxygen-redox reversibility.

records.title: An extra beat every minute
records.description: Small deviations in the power system frequency are routinely attributed to stochastic fluctuations in load and generation. New research reveals a disturbance recurring precisely every minute in grids worldwide, caused by clock-synchronized self-tests in battery-based uninterruptible power supplies that inadvertently act in unison.

records.title: Durable reactive CO 2 capture exceeding 1,000 h via self-reinforcing molecular catalysts
records.description: Reactive CO 2 capture integrates carbon capture and electrochemical conversion in a single process, but poor catalyst durability remains a major challenge. Here the authors show that pH-swing-driven acidification accelerates catalyst demetallation and develop a cobalt phthalocyanine catalyst that suppresses metal loss, sustaining efficient CO production for 1,000 h.

records.title: Caloric cooling devices and systems
records.description: Caloric cooling offers a promising solid-state alternative to conventional refrigeration, but system-level challenges continue to limit practical deployment. This Review evaluates the state of the art, identifies the key barriers to scalable devices and outlines a roadmap for sustainable cooling.

records.title: One-minute frequency disturbances from unintended synchronization in cyber–physical power systems
records.description: Power grids on five continents show frequency oscillations with a period of exactly 1 min. The authors trace this to clock-synchronized software in devices such as uninterruptible power supplies that creates coherent, repeating demand peaks.

records.title: Translating sulfur flow batteries into deployable systems
records.description: Sulfur-based redox flow batteries promise low-cost, long-duration energy storage using abundant active materials, but commercial success depends on much more than low-cost materials. Yi-Chun Lu and her team explore how deployment reshapes research priorities and reveals the scientific and engineering bottlenecks that determine technology translation.

records.title: Chemical-linkage-regulated single-phase crystallization and uniform gallium alloying for efficient solution-processed chalcopyrite solar cells
records.description: Controlling phase evolution and composition homogeneity are challenging for chalcopyrites. Ma, Wu, Liu, Yan et al. use acetate anions to build complex networks in precursor solution, achieving single-phase crystallization and an 18.53% efficient Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 solar cell.

records.title: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics
records.description: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells are promising for high area-normalized power output, but factors governing the photothermal stability of perovskite absorbers remains unclear. Xu et al. identify lattice compliance as a descriptor when screening stable perovskites.

records.title: Structural improvements to address energy poverty had most substantial thermal comfort and health effects
records.description: Energy poverty is a growing concern, but we still know little about which measures actually improve people’s health and living conditions. Here the authors find that structural measures and consistent financial support deliver the clearest benefits.

records.title: Heatwave-induced capacity bottlenecks in European electricity grids
records.description: This study models how heatwaves raise demand and reduce generation and transmission capacity across Western European power grids, showing how heatwaves can expose bottlenecks that simplified models may miss and providing a basis for resilience planning.

records.title: Directed assembly of cathode interlayers enables efficient binary organic solar cells
records.description: Cathode interlayers play a pivotal role in improving the performance of organic solar cells. Yao, Zhang, Zhang, Wang et al. show a stepwise solvent treatment to achieve a vertically aligned cathode interlayer, enabling a certified efficiency of 20.65% in binary organic solar cells.

records.title: All-organic mixed-matrix membranes with single-crystal covalent organic frameworks for carbon capture
records.description: Carbon capture with conventional mixed-matrix membranes is limited by the inability to achieve high packing densities of porous fillers while preserving their intrinsic transport properties. Here the authors develop high-performance membranes based on single-crystal covalent organic framework fillers using a weak-interaction inlaying strategy that enables high filler loadings.

records.title: From gigawatts to critical mineral demands for EU solar and wind
records.description: Clean energy systems rely on large amounts of minerals. Here the researchers show that meeting EU solar and wind targets will create high demand for copper, zinc, silicon and rare earth elements, especially when offshore wind remains central.

records.title: A Ni(OH) 2 symmetric battery cell for hydroxide exchange membrane-based direct air capture of CO 2
records.description: Electrochemical carbon capture promises low-energy direct air capture (DAC), but demonstrations are often confined to small devices and short lifetimes. Here the authors report a 25-cm 2 symmetric nickel hydroxide DAC cell operated for 5,000 h at a low energy cost and demonstrate scale-up to a 9 × 300 cm 2 stack.

records.title: Rethink data centre planning
records.description: The rapid expansion of data centres is challenging power systems and planning processes to keep pace.

records.title: Spatially informed policies can accelerate green hydrogen demand
records.description: Realized green hydrogen demand lags behind policy targets but could be accelerated by accounting for spatial spillovers, which refer to demand-side interdependencies where adoption by one user encourages further adoption by nearby users. Revising EU green hydrogen policies, including Hydrogen Valleys and European Hydrogen Bank auctions, to better account for these location-specific demand-side patterns could improve their effectiveness.

records.title: Spatially informed demand-side policies for green hydrogen diffusion in Europe
records.description: EU green hydrogen policies could be more effective if they accounted for spatial spillovers. These spillovers are a primary driver of diffusion, and spatially informed demand-side policies could improve cost-effectiveness by up to 41%.

records.title: Smart energy must address enshittification risks
A unified distillation and electrolysis system
records.description: Seawater is an attractive feedstock for hydrogen production that overcomes community concerns about fresh water; however, electrolysis of seawater remains challenging. Now, a coupled alkaline water electrolysis and vacuum distillation in a unified process overcomes those challenges by using waste heat to treat seawater, enabling 250 kW-scale efficient co-production of hydrogen and fresh water.

records.title: A 250-kilowatt system for co-production of hydrogen and fresh water from seawater
records.description: Given its abundance, seawater is an attractive feedstock for hydrogen production, but direct electrolysis is hindered by side reactions and corrosion. Here the authors couple alkaline electrolysis with low-temperature desalination, using waste electrolyser heat to distil seawater into a fresh water feed, enabling stable, scalable performance.

records.title: Exploring hydrogen pipeline costs by considering regional geographical and political characteristics
records.description: Hydrogen pipelines could become important for future energy systems, but current cost estimates often ignore regional differences. This study develops a more realistic approach that accounts for geography, infrastructure and financing factors to improve hydrogen transport cost assessments.

records.title: A hidden leak in solids
records.description: Solid electrolytes have long been treated as materials that block electronic conduction while enabling fast lithium-ion transport. Two studies now show that residual electronic conductivity can drive self-discharge in solid-state batteries at open circuit, particularly in thin practical cells, and identify the limits needed to ensure long shelf life.

records.title: Halogen-assisted sulfur oxidation
records.description: Lithium-sulfur batteries have long been limited by lower operating voltage and shorter lifetime compared to traditional lithium-ion technologies. Now, system-level engineering enables the conversion of sulfur to disulfur dichloride, accessing the S +1 oxidation state, thereby delivering higher voltage and improved cycling stability.

records.title: Ironing out the wrinkles
records.description: Ultrawide-bandgap perovskites are essential for all-perovskite triple-junction solar cells, yet their high bromide content causes surface wrinkling and halide disorder, limiting the performance. A surface reconstruction and halide homogenization strategy now enables a certified efficiency of 29.3% in all-perovskite triple-junction devices.

records.title: Integrated photovoltaics need design innovation and cross-sector collaboration
Lithium–disulfur dichloride batteries
records.description: Rechargeable Li–S batteries offer high energy density but are limited by low voltage, sluggish kinetics and polysulfide shuttling. Here the authors report a chlorine-mediated Li||S 2 Cl 2 chemistry enabling reversible three-electron sulfur redox with increased voltage and capacity.

records.title: Crystallization control of 2.0-eV bandgap perovskites for all-perovskite triple-junction solar cells
records.description: Ultrawide-bandgap perovskites suffer from heterogeneities during crystallization. Zhang et al. use solvent and additive engineering to smooth the process for 2.0-eV bandgap perovskites, enabling 30.1% efficiency in all-perovskite triple-junction solar cells.

records.title: A heat-driven route to elastocaloric cooling
records.description: A heat-driven elastocaloric cooling system is demonstrated in which two shape memory alloys perform complementary roles: one converts heat into mechanical work, while the other converts that work into cooling. This approach offers a pathway to electricity-minimized solid-state cooling using abundant low-grade heat sources.

records.title: Applying causal machine learning to assess and improve cleantech policy design
records.description: Effective clean technology (cleantech) policies, such as subsidies and carbon pricing, require an understanding of how interventions shape environmental and socioeconomic outcomes. To support targeted, evidence-based policy design, we discuss how causal machine learning can compare alternative policy scenarios and reveal where, how and for whom cleantech policies work.

records.title: Quasi-ballistic ion transport boosts evaporation-driven electricity generation
records.description: Evaporation-driven electricity generation can utilize the abundant thermal energy in the atmosphere, but is limited by ion scattering in the energy-harvesting material. Machine learning has now enabled the design of vertical microrod generators that achieve quasi-ballistic ion transport, boosting the power density and power conversion efficiency.

records.title: Industrializing reactive capture of CO 2
records.description: Reactive capture of CO 2 integrates capture and conversion, bypassing regeneration and potentially simplifying upstream–downstream process integration, but its deployment readiness is unclear. In this Perspective the authors argue that reactive capture of CO 2 could be industrially viable at present levels of selectivity and voltage if stability and scale barriers are addressed.

records.title: Heat-driven elastocaloric cooling with shape memory films
records.description: Elastocaloric cooling in shape memory alloy films is efficient but limited by electrically powered actuators. Here the authors demonstrate a heat-driven system that achieves a temperature span of up to 12.9 K (4.0 K at device level), showing that waste heat can be used for electricity-minimized cooling.

records.title: Quantifying the impact of cell-to-cell inconsistency on electric vehicle battery degradation and utilization
records.description: Cell-to-cell inconsistency is a key barrier to realizing full performance in electric vehicle batteries. Using large-scale real-world fleet data, the researchers quantify its impact and show considerable losses in battery health, pack lifetime, power capability and usable energy.

records.title: Iron-mediated reversible lattice-oxygen redox enables stable 200 Wh kg −1 sodium-ion batteries
records.description: Lattice-oxygen redox can raise the energy density of layered oxide cathodes, but poor reversibility causes structural degradation and capacity loss. Here the authors use iron as a bulk redox mediator to boost oxygen-redox reversibility and stabilize high-energy sodium-ion batteries.

records.title: Best practices for measuring the performance and stability of indoor photovoltaic devices
records.description: A major challenge for indoor photovoltaics is the absence of harmonized testing protocols, standards, and shared performance benchmarks. This Consensus Statement outlines recommended practices for testing and reporting device performance, power, efficiency and stability.

records.title: Interface engineering towards high-efficiency perovskite/CIGS tandem solar cells
records.description: The efficiency of perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells has been limited by interfacial challenges. Now, a dual-interface engineering strategy enables conformal perovskite coverage on textured CIGS bottom-cell surfaces while increasing carrier extraction at the electron‑ and hole‑transport interfaces. This strategy enables monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandems with a power conversion efficiency of >30% and good stability.

records.title: Diffusionless mechanisms produce diffusion-like electrochemistry in battery particles
records.description: Overpotentials at low frequencies in Li-ion battery active particles have long been attributed to solid diffusion. Now, electrolyte penetration in battery agglomerate particles is shown to make interior surfaces electrochemically active, but with a transmission-line configuration. This mechanism for accessing battery capacity produces diffusion-like electrochemistry, even without diffusion involved.

records.title: Economic and behavioural policy coupling has divergent effects on electric vehicle adoption at individual and system scales
records.description: Policy mixes are widely used to accelerate low-carbon transitions, but their effects across different levels are unclear. Here the researchers show that a carbon tax and information intervention additively boost individual electric vehicle adoption but have divergent effects on system-level electric vehicle uptake and policy support.

records.title: Electronic conductivity of solid electrolytes causes physical self-discharge in all-solid-state batteries
records.description: Physical self-discharge critically limits the lifetime of all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). Wang et al. showed that the non-negligible electronic conductivity of solid-state electrolytes can lead to substantial physical self-discharge in ASSBs.

records.title: Author Correction: High-performance perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells enabled by multifunctional titanium oxynitride recombination layers
Improving interface-mediated carrier transport for efficient perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 tandem solar cells
records.description: The performance of perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 tandem solar cells is limited by optical and electronic losses at the interfaces between layers. By engineering two of these interfaces, Zeng, Wang, Tang et al. achieve a certified efficiency of 30.57% and improved device stability.

records.title: Coordinating EV charging modes and energy system planning reveals uneven savings across Europe
records.description: Including the costs of charging infrastructure in a European energy system model reveals that unidirectional smart charging delivers up to 4.5% in annual system cost savings, whereas bidirectional charging technology generates substantial market revenues in solar-dominated systems. Thus, charging infrastructure targets should account for differences across diverse national energy systems.

records.title: Diffusion-like overpotentials from non-diffusion mechanisms in battery particles
records.description: Low-frequency electrochemical responses in lithium-ion battery electrodes are widely interpreted as signatures of solid-state lithium diffusion. Here the authors show that electrolyte penetration in porous cathode particles can generate similar diffusion-like behaviour independent of bulk diffusion.

records.title: From takeout to takeoff
records.description: Converting plastic waste into jet fuel could help decarbonize aviation, but upcycling routes often require high pressures and long reaction times. New research demonstrates that catalysts based on atomically-dispersed Ru atoms on oxide supports can rapidly convert waste plastics into jet fuel components under mild conditions.

records.title: Quasi-ballistic ion transport in a vertical microrod enabling efficient evaporation-driven power generation
records.description: Evaporation-driven power generators are often limited by non-directional fluid flow, which reduces their efficiency. Guided by machine learning, Wu et al. developed a vertical microrod generator that improves ion transport, increasing efficiency and power density.

records.title: High-performance perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells enabled by multifunctional titanium oxynitride recombination layers
records.description: The interconnected recombination layer is key to advance perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells. Cao et al. show that titanium oxynitride reconciles the requirements for recombination layers, improving the efficiency and stability for tandem solar cells and modules.

records.title: Low-temperature oxide-ion conduction in Aurivillius-type ((Na 0.5 Bi 0.5 ) n –1 Ti n O 3 n )(Bi 2 O 2 ) phases
records.description: Solid oxide-ion conductors are essential for high-temperature electrochemical technologies, yet few materials maintain sufficient ion mobility at lower temperatures, where degradation is reduced and a broader range of materials can be used for auxiliary components. Here the authors introduce Aurivillius-type thin-film conductors that form periodic fast ion channels and achieve promising conductivity at 350 °C.

records.title: Towards technology-smart green industrial policy
records.description: Identifying future winning energy technologies is increasingly important as governments design green industrial policy. By evaluating technology characteristics, policymakers can strategically pick winning technologies that deliver both global cost-competitiveness and domestic economic payoffs.

records.title: Challenges and trends in automotive battery recycling
records.description: The rapid growth of electric vehicles is creating a surge of end-of-life batteries. This Review evaluates current recycling methods, their suitability for emerging chemistries and the practical challenges for scaling a circular battery industry.

records.title: Building chemical stability with mechanics
records.description: Stack pressure strongly influences degradation pathways in lithium-ion batteries, yet its optimal value remains poorly understood. Now, a high-precision stack pressure control and dilatometry system reveals an optimal pressure window that suppresses key degradation pathways and doubles battery lifetime.

records.title: Climate change reshapes resource adequacy risks and optimal renewable energy siting in wind and solar energy systems
records.description: Decarbonized grids may face rising resource adequacy risks as weather-driven renewable variability and climate change jointly affect supply and demand. A high-resolution model shows that these risks stem from multi-day power shortfalls and system design, but can be reduced through region-specific, climate-informed siting and transmission planning.

records.title: Author Correction: Thin membranes with Cu-ion crosslinking for high temperature polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells
Coordinated planning of European charging infrastructure and energy system for optimal V1G and V2G deployment
records.description: European charging infrastructure targets rely on uniform benchmarks that overlook flexibility from smart charging (V1G) and V2G. A system model shows that V1G delivers most cost and infrastructure savings, whereas V2G provides smaller savings but substantial balancing revenues, particularly in photovoltaic-dominated, grid-constrained systems.

records.title: Controlled solid-state crystallization with formamidinium acetate for fully vacuum-deposited perovskite solar cells
records.description: Vacuum-processed perovskite solar cells show promise, yet their efficiency remains limited. Xu et al. use formamidinium acetate to promote perovskite crystallization, achieving a 25.5% power conversion efficiency and 1,000 h operational stability.

records.title: Ligand-confined zinc slurries enable durable flow-based energy storage
records.description: Zinc-based batteries could offer long-duration energy storage, yet conventional zinc electrodes degrade during cycling. Now, a flowing zinc slurry battery is developed with zinc nanoparticles dispersed in a conductive network and a ligand that stabilizes the slurry. The slurry shows reversible Zn/Zn 2+ conversion and enables durable battery operation.

records.title: Early-stage local chemistry regulation enabling open-circuit voltage of 847 mV in wide-bandgap Cu 2 ZnSnS 4 solar cells
records.description: Elemental diffusion in Cu 2 ZnSnS 4 induces secondary phases and defects, limiting the open-circuit voltage in associated solar cells. Wang et al. introduce two-stage copper incorporation to suppress copper out-diffusion, enabling 12.4% efficiency and an 874-mV open-circuit voltage in solar cells.

records.title: Managing the impacts of EU electric vehicle import tariffs
records.description: EU import tariffs on battery electric vehicles may not substantially hinder the overall electrification process but may substantially reduce adoption in vulnerable markets. These findings highlight the uneven implications of broad trade interventions and underscore the importance of complementary policies to support a resilient and inclusive transition.

records.title: Distributional impacts of EU tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles across European markets
records.description: Tariffs have been introduced in the EU on battery electric vehicles (EVs) imported from China. New research considers how these tariffs may lead to cost increases and reshape EV adoption across the EU.

records.title: Household coordination can aid solar adoption
records.description: Coordination and active deliberation that includes the whole household can facilitate solar adoption. Interventions targeting energy adoption are likely to be more effective when they are designed to support collective decision making rather than focusing on a single member of the household.

records.title: Family dynamics are a missing piece in understanding residential solar adoption
records.description: Household-wide coordination capacity underpins residential solar adoption. In-sync households share goals, actively deliberate and act collectively to adopt. Oppositional households are misaligned, face coordination snags and do not adopt.

records.title: Critical surface strain regime for stable and active epitaxial platinum oxygen reduction electrocatalysts
records.description: Manipulating surface strain in epitaxial transition metal films can enhance electrocatalytic activity, yet maintaining long-term performance is challenging due to irreversible strain relaxation. Here the authors identify a thickness-dependent critical strain in epitaxial Pt/Ir films that optimizes stability and activity for the oxygen reduction reaction.

records.title: The interplay between stack pressure, mechanical expansion and degradation pathways in lithium-ion batteries
records.description: While electrochemical degradation in lithium-ion batteries is well studied, the role of stack pressure in long-term cycling remains unclear. Here the researchers use a high-precision pressure-controlled dilatometry tool to optimize stack pressure and understand how it prolongs battery lifetime.

records.title: Accessible solar tower power plant data to accelerate solar energy research
records.description: Over 800 GB of high-resolution operational solar tower power plant data have been compiled to form an open-access interface that complies with FAIR data principles. This database, known as PAINT, democratizes access to structured operational data, with the goal of facilitating the development of data-driven solutions in solar tower research.

records.title: Mitigation of hydrogen crossover in liquid alkaline water electrolysers using gas recombination catalysts
records.description: Alkaline water electrolysers are being optimized for higher performance, but measures such as advanced electrodes or thinner separators can increase hydrogen crossover and safety risks. Here the authors analyse crossover behaviour and show that a gas recombination catalyst cuts crossover by 95% without affecting electrolyser performance.

records.title: A coloured radiative cooling coating with high solar reflectance
records.description: Overcoming the trade-off between colouration and high solar reflectance is a challenge for radiative cooling materials. Now, an ethyl cellulose coating fabricated in one step achieves vibrant structural colours with negligible solar absorption and high long-wave infrared emission. This coating enables sub-ambient daytime cooling of up to 9 °C under sunlight.

records.title: A cascade hole-transfer strategy towards stable hybrid perovskite solar cells
records.description: Perovskite solar cells are a leading candidate for next-generation commercial photovoltaics, but their sensitivity to heat and moisture limits their practical use. Now, a cascade hole-transfer strategy is developed to suppress charge recombination in hybrid perovskite/organic solar cells while offering intrinsic moisture stability.

records.title: Batteries versus fuel cells for decarbonizing medium- and heavy-duty vehicles across applications
records.description: Decarbonizing medium- and heavy-duty vehicles is challenging, and the relative benefits of batteries versus fuel cells remain uncertain across applications. This modelling work shows that both reduce emissions versus diesel, but battery electric vehicles powered by renewable electricity deliver the lowest life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions in most cases.

records.title: Quantifying X-ray damage
Interacting causes of mini-grid failure
Open-air perovskite fabrication
Flowing zinc slurry for long-duration energy storage
records.description: Aqueous Zn batteries are attractive for low-cost and safe energy storage, yet their practical use is hindered by limited reversibility. Here the authors report a ligand-confined, flowable Zn slurry that enables durable and efficient operation.

records.title: Scaling vanadium flow battery for long-duration energy storage
records.description: Despite early promise, vanadium flow batteries struggled to move beyond pilot projects due to bottlenecks that emerged at scale. Overcoming these barriers to enable reliable, cost-effective long-duration energy storage at multi-hundred-megawatt scale is discussed by Xianfeng Li and colleagues.

records.title: The PAINT database for operational concentrating solar power plant data following FAIR data principles
records.description: The limited availability of operational data slows the development of concentrating solar power. To address this issue, Phipps et al. developed PAINT, a FAIR, open-access database that compiles multi-year data from a plant in Jülich, Germany.

records.title: Industrial overcapacity can enable seasonal flexibility in electricity use
records.description: Lyu et al. show that industrial overcapacity, long viewed as a burden, can be repurposed. Using China’s aluminium sector as an example, they demonstrate that excess capacity and material storage can provide seasonal flexibility to lower energy costs.

records.title: Watching catalysis take a walk
records.description: Electrocatalytic surfaces are dynamic, but few methods correlate nanometre-scale current with structure across large areas. Interferometric electro-optical microscopy now images electrochemical currents at 50 nm and 10 ms resolution, revealing that hydrogen evolution on MoS 2 initiates and propagates along specific crystallographic directions.

records.title: Author Correction: Stable tin–lead perovskite inks for efficient all-perovskite tandems
Understanding interconnected ion and water transport in anion exchange membrane zero-gap CO 2 electrolysers
records.description: Achieving long-term stability in low-temperature anion exchange membrane zero-gap CO 2 electrolysers is hindered by salt precipitation and flooding, which limit CO 2 transport. In this Perspective, the authors explore the interplay between ion and water transport processes, emphasizing the need for strategies to simultaneously manage both to extend cell runtimes.

records.title: Aligning global shipping climate policies with life cycle perspective
records.description: The IMO Net-Zero Framework promotes adoption of low climate impact marine fuel through combination of pricing mechanism and fuel standard; however, fuel choice depends on competition for clean energy across sectors. Policies must consider life cycle perspective to avoid shifting impacts to the fuel supply chain and address wider environmental impacts, including land use and mineral resource depletion.

records.title: Marine fuel choices and related life-cycle environmental impacts under global shipping policies
records.description: Shipping is a hard-to-decarbonize sector that is competing for energy and requires effective policies to cut emissions. This study shows that combining fuel standards and levies speeds up the adoption of low-carbon fuels such as ammonia but may increase other environmental impacts.

records.title: Energy use in AI responses
Controlling phase separation
Flowing hot and cold
Ambient-pressure conversion of plastic waste to jet fuel cycloalkanes by tandem hydropyrolysis and vapour-phase hydrogenation
records.description: Converting plastic waste into jet fuel could support aviation decarbonization, but current approaches are limited by high-pressure requirements and low efficiency. Here the authors present a tandem hydropyrolysis and vapour-phase hydrogenation strategy that uses a Ru/Co-Al oxide catalyst, achieving promising rates and yields at low pressures.

records.title: Stable tin–lead perovskite inks for efficient all-perovskite tandems
records.description: Low-bandgap tin–lead perovskites can boost solar cell efficiency but degrade quickly due to tin oxidation. Here the authors add proton-scavenging additives that stabilize inks for over 300 days, enabling 24.06% single cells and 29.56% certified tandem efficiency.

records.title: Reimagining energy research and education
A thin and robust polymer electrolyte membrane with dynamic metal-ion crosslinking
records.description: Dynamic copper-ion crosslinking of polybenzimidazole yields a thin yet mechanically robust polymer electrolyte membrane. Fuel cells incorporating this membrane achieve a high peak power density and exhibit good stability at elevated temperatures.

records.title: Additive-assisted liquid medium annealing relieving strains in perovskite solar cells for improved stability
records.description: The annealing process introduces strain into the perovskite and undermines the stability of the solar cells. Xiaofeng Gao et al. address this issue by using a meltable additive, 1,4-butanesultam, to relieve strain and improve operational stability.

records.title: Resilient electricity infrastructure and energy transitions in island states
records.description: Nature Energy talks to Paul Bertheau, Head of the Research Unit Off-Grid Systems at the Reiner-Lemoine-Institut, about challenges and approaches to enhancing resilience in island states when it comes to electricity and energy access in the transition away from fossil fuels.

records.title: CO 2 -enabled recovery
records.description: Cation contamination has long hindered deployment of highly active platinum-alloy catalysts in commercial proton exchange membrane fuel cells. Now, a CO 2 -assisted recovery protocol allows contaminants to be removed from inside an operating cell, potentially redefining the practical outlook for platinum-alloy catalysts.

records.title: A twist away from hydrogen
records.description: Electron spins are often not considered in electrocatalysis, yet they can play a pivotal role in determining reaction pathways. New research suggests that chiral (twisted) copper can generate spin-polarized charge carriers during CO 2 electroreduction and suppress undesired hydrogen evolution.

records.title: Securing US electric vehicle battery supply requires domestic action and international sourcing
records.description: Expanding domestic production and implementing demand-side strategies can substantially narrow material shortages for US electric vehicle batteries, but these efforts still fall short of meeting projected 2035 demand. To assure US battery supplies, the USA must support investments across all domestic supply chain stages, reduce and shift battery material demand, and continue to secure international supplies.

records.title: Improving the stability of monolithic perovskite/silicon tandems against reverse-bias stress using graded dielectric layers
records.description: Perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells degrade under reverse bias. Wang et al. introduce graded dielectric layers that smooth the electric field and reduce tunnelling and interfacial reactions, improving reverse-bias tolerance.

records.title: Evaluating strategies to address material supply–demand gaps in the US electric vehicle battery supply chain
records.description: As the USA works to secure supplies of electric vehicle battery materials, Lu et al. show that this will require investment across the domestic supply chain, demand-side strategies and continued international sourcing.

records.title: Anion-reduction catalytic centres regulate interfacial solvation structures for fast-charging Si anodes
records.description: Interfacial solvation structures are key to stable fast charging in Si anodes. Qiao and colleagues show that S-vacancy-driven anion-reduction catalysis regulates these structures to form a LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase, enabling ultrafast charging and long cycle life.

records.title: Close-space sublimation as a versatile deposition process for efficient perovskite silicon tandem solar cells
records.description: Research on perovskite solar cells shows that scaling up production will require faster, more reliable film-making methods. This work introduces a simple high-rate process that forms high-quality wide-bandgap films for efficient single-junction and tandem devices.

records.title: A balanced approach to oxygen electrodes
records.description: Although reversible solid oxide cells show promise for clean energy conversion, performance and stability is still limited by their oxygen electrodes. New work demonstrates a design that accelerates oxygen exchange by targeting balanced transport of oxide ions and electrons.

records.title: An Australian government scheme holds potential for supporting a just energy transition
Hole-transfer cascade-engineered donor polymer for unencapsulated perovskite solar cells with improved moisture stability
records.description: Moisture stability is a challenge for perovskite solar cells. Min-Ho Lee et al. design an electron-donating polymer with a deep highest occupied molecular orbital that enhances the devices’ resistance to moisture.

records.title: Perceived societal and environmental impacts, fairness and emotions predict policy support in Europe
records.description: Energy policy support hinges on public perceptions of the impacts of these policies on society and the environment, of how fair impacts are, and on policy-related emotions. These aspects should be given priority when designing and communicating new policies.

records.title: Predictors of informed energy policy support across Europe
records.description: New research finds that across Europe, peoples’ perceptions of the societal and environmental impact and the distributional fairness of an energy policy, together with the emotions experienced towards the policy, are strongly related to policy support.

records.title: Unlocking hidden sodium
records.description: Fe-based polyanionic cathodes are promising for large-scale Na-ion batteries but are limited by incomplete Na utilization. Now, research shows that tuning the local Na coordination via V substitution in phosphate-based cathode allows additional Na sites to participate, enabling near-complete Na utilization, enhancing energy density and cycling stability.

records.title: Harmonized sodium coordination engineering for high-energy phosphate cathodes
records.description: Fe-based polyanionic cathodes are promising for Na-ion batteries but are limited by inactive Na sites and irreversible Na loss. Here the authors employ targeted V 3+ substitution to tune the Na + coordination environment, activate inert sites and stabilize high-voltage redox for high-performance Na-ion batteries.

records.title: Chirality-induced spin selectivity as a mechanism to control product selectivity during electrochemical CO 2 reduction
records.description: Electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction is often hindered by the competing hydrogen evolution reaction, reducing selectivity for the desired products. Here the authors demonstrate that helical chiral copper electrodes can suppress hydrogen evolution by generating spin-polarized carriers through the chiral-induced spin selectivity effect.

records.title: Molecular-templated pre-assembly of self-assembled monolayer for perovskite solar cells and modules with improved reverse-bias stability
records.description: Perovskite solar modules suffer from reverse-bias instability. To address this, Wang et al. promote the assembly of self-assembled monolayers through hydrogen-bonding interactions with a polycarbazole template.

records.title: Integrated planning of net-zero power systems for all
records.description: New research introduces a global, high-resolution power system model to show that achieving a net-zero electricity sector while ensuring equitable access to decent living standards is both technically feasible and economically viable by mid-century.

records.title: Composite air electrodes based on BaCe 0.7 Zr 0.1 Y 0.1 Yb 0.1 O 3− δ for reversible solid oxide cells
records.description: Reversible solid oxide cells can be limited by the kinetics of the reactions occurring at the oxygen electrode. Here the authors show that compositing a Gd 0.3 Ca 2.7 Co 3.82 Cu 0.18 O 9− δ catalyst with a balanced oxygen-ion- and hole-conducting BaCe 1− x Zr x O 3 -based material leads to enhancements in performance.

records.title: Oxygen-tolerant electrochemical CO 2 separation using N-heterocyclic imines with superstoichiometric release per electron
records.description: Electrochemically mediated CO 2 capture typically makes use of sorbents that must be reduced before binding CO 2 , a process often hampered by competitive oxygen reduction reactions. Here the authors develop N-heterocyclic imines that capture CO 2 in the neutral state and release it with near-theoretical Faradaic efficiency upon electro-oxidation, avoiding the competing reaction.

records.title: Pushing tunnel oxide passivating contact technology
records.description: As silicon solar cells approach their theoretical efficiency limit, further performance gains become increasingly difficult. Two studies now demonstrate advances in mainstream tunnel oxide passivating contact technology: one improves the boron emitter and polysilicon in the standard design, while the other proposes an alternative cell architecture that overcomes limitations of the mainstream approach.

records.title: An analytical model to describe self-discharge rates in solid-state batteries
records.description: Internal self-discharge can compromise the shelf life of solid-state batteries. Now, physico-chemical analysis of charge loss shows that the internal self-discharge over time is not solely determined by the electronic conductivity of the solid separator but also by its electrochemical stability. This model could help guide separator and cell design.

records.title: Thin membranes with Cu-ion crosslinking for high temperature polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells
records.description: High-temperature polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells tend to use relatively thick membranes to counteract H 3 PO 4 -induced degradation, limiting performance. Here the authors introduce a dynamic metal-ion crosslinking strategy to create thin, robust membranes, achieving promising power density and durability.

records.title: Water-based membranes
Sodium is not lithium
Mitigating lead toxicity towards safer commercialization of perovskite solar cells
records.description: The presence of lead in perovskite photovoltaics requires careful scrutiny before commercialization. In this Review Lin and colleagues discuss mitigation strategies and the end-of-life implications for recycling and sustainability.

records.title: Imaging dynamic electrocatalytic processes on nano-strained MoS 2 using interferometric electro-optical microscopy
records.description: Understanding dynamic heterogeneity in hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts is essential but difficult with limited spatio-temporal resolution. Here the authors use interferometric electro-optical microscopy to achieve nanometre–millisecond imaging of hydrogen evolution activity on MoS 2 .

records.title: War in the Middle East hands Europe another chance to break its fossil fuel dependency
Quantifying the self-discharge rate of solid-state batteries
records.description: Internal self-discharge limits solid-state batteries because chemical potential differences drive ions and electrons to move across the separator, causing charge loss during storage. Here Janek and Alt present an analytical model that shows how tiny electronic leaks in the solid separator can cause reversible self-discharge, providing guidance for separator and cell design.

records.title: Author Correction: Probabilistic projections of global wind and solar power growth based on historical national experience
Reactive CO 2 capture via controlled amine speciation in non-aqueous electrolytes
records.description: The integration of carbon capture and electrochemical conversion is an emerging strategy to valorize CO 2 . Here the authors demonstrate that altering CO 2 –amine speciation in aprotic media enhances CO 2 uptake and suppresses hydrogen evolution, achieving promising Faradaic efficiency towards CO production, including with flue gas feedstocks.

records.title: A scalable, biopolymer-based microenvironment for electrochemical CO 2 conversion to multicarbon products with current densities over 2 A cm − 2
records.description: Electrochemical CO 2 reduction to multicarbon products is hindered by difficulties in microenvironment control at high current densities. Here the authors demonstrate that biopolymer coatings on electrocatalysts enhance local conditions, achieving high Faradaic efficiencies and challenging assumptions about the need for hydrophobic materials in such systems.

records.title: Grid access and electricity for refugees
records.description: Sarah Rosenberg-Jansen is a senior research fellow at the Stockholm Environment Institute, where she conducts research on UN institutional policies and private-sector practices on sustainable energy and climate within humanitarian systems and refugee camps. She speaks to Nature Energy about refugee grid and electricity access in forced displacement settings.

records.title: Why Europe’s solar rollout must account for the solar rebound effect
records.description: When households install rooftop solar panels, they often increase their electricity consumption due to the perception of ‘free’ energy, a phenomenon known as the solar rebound effect. Energy scenarios should reflect this additional demand, while associated policy should incentivize use during sunny hours to limit system costs and unfair cost shifting.

records.title: Implications of the solar rebound effect for the European energy transition
records.description: When households install solar panels, they often increase electricity use due to the energy they perceive as ‘free’. This study shows how this so-called solar rebound effect shapes Europe’s energy system, driving investment needs and costs, and calls for inclusion in planning.

records.title: Probabilistic projections of global wind and solar power growth based on historical national experience
records.description: PROLONG, a data-driven probabilistic model of technology growth, projects wind and solar expansion consistent with 2 °C pathways and faster than current policy scenarios. The 1.5 °C pathway lies beyond the 95th percentile of projections and meeting this target would require major effort.

records.title: Unlocking the potential of the insulator–metal transition for photocatalysis
records.description: Designing photocatalysts typically demands complex engineering of junctions. Vanadium dioxide (VO 2 ), however, can spontaneously form homogeneous junctions upon undergoing an insulator–metal transition. This transition in VO 2 thin films under light increases the photocatalytic conversion rate of methane into hydrogen and light alkanes.

records.title: One-step-processed bilayer ethyl cellulose for full-colour sub-ambient daytime radiative cooling
records.description: Fabricating coloured radiative cooling coatings that are easy to produce and do not compromise cooling performance is challenging. Ying Liu et al. develop a one-step fabrication method that yields coloured ethyl cellulose coatings while preserving high solar reflectance.

records.title: Calendar ageing of micro-sized silicon
records.description: Silicon anodes promise far higher capacity than graphite but suffer from rapid decay at rest. Researchers evaluate cycling stability and calendar life of micron-sized silicon anodes after tuning electrolytes to form a LiF-rich solid–electrolyte interphase and propose a metric to assess calendar ageing.

records.title: Addressing the challenge of carbon dioxide in anion-exchange membrane fuel cells
records.description: Anion-exchange membrane fuel cells (AEMFCs) face performance challenges due to CO 2 in ambient air, which forms carbonate ions that reduce ionic conductivity. In this Perspective, the authors explore CO 2 management strategies and discuss its potential stabilizing effects, offering insights to enhance AEMFC performance and stability.

records.title: Governance challenges preventing better integration of the electrical grid in the USA
records.description: The USA’s electricity network remains underdeveloped and fragmented in ways that threaten the reliability, resilience and affordability of electricity as well as clean energy goals. The design of its grid governance is largely to blame for insufficient investment in electricity transmission, making governance reforms a critical precondition to constructing a stronger grid.

records.title: Thermal runaway-free ampere-hour-level Na-ion battery via polymerizable non-flammable electrolyte
records.description: The safe operation of large-scale batteries remains challenging, as thermal runaway in ampere-hour-level cells is still unresolved and the link between electrolyte flame retardancy and battery safety is unclear. Here the authors report a polymerizable non-flammable electrolyte that forms a protective cross-linked barrier, suppresses side reactions and prevents thermal runaway.

records.title: Fusion power unlikely to become competitive
records.description: While nuclear fusion power is often hailed as a future source of abundant, clean energy, current dominant fusion designs, magnetic and laser inertial, are unlikely to become competitive due to their expected low experience rates. Accordingly, policymakers should not rely on, or fund, fusion power as a core pillar of future clean energy systems unless designs with different characteristics are developed.

records.title: Degradation pathways of FA x Cs 1− x PbI 3 perovskite solar cells
records.description: The upper stability limit of formamidinium–caesium (FACs) lead iodide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) under thermal and light stress is poorly understood. Now, analysis of the photothermal stability of hundreds of FACs PSCs reveals distinct temperature-dependent degradation modes. On the basis of the mechanistic insight, stabilizing strategies are proposed to mitigate the degradation pathways.

records.title: Understanding reverse bias effects
records.description: Perovskite photovoltaics that use self-assembled monolayers as hole-transport layers are unstable under reverse bias, but the underlying mechanism has not been well understood. This instability is now shown to arise from formamidinium deprotonation triggered by the discontinuities in the self-assembled monolayer on the indium tin oxide substrate.

records.title: Standardized framework enables municipal energy access and energy poverty action globally
records.description: The Energy Access and Energy Poverty Pillar framework may enable municipalities worldwide to operationalize energy interventions relating to security, sustainability and affordability. Voluntarily reported municipal data and local contextual knowledge should be used together to expand energy access and energy poverty policies, with coordination across governance levels supporting this process.

records.title: Progress on urban energy access and energy poverty in the Global Covenant of Mayors initiative
records.description: This study presents the Global Covenant of Mayors Energy Access and Poverty Pillar and analyses its first-year implementation across 1,354 municipalities that account for 296 million people, revealing adoption patterns and sectoral priorities.

records.title: Controlled Cs⁺ incorporation through organocaesium salts in α-FA–Cs perovskite solar cells with a certified efficiency of 26.61%
records.description: The formation of α-phase formamidinium–caesium metal halide perovskites is hindered by limited Cs⁺ incorporation. He et al. use caesium 4-(diphenylphosphino)benzoate to enable efficient Cs⁺ doping and achieve solar cells with an efficiency of 26.6%.

records.title: Quasi-random oriented molecular contacts for inverted perovskite solar cells with improved efficiency
records.description: Self-assembled hole-selective molecules can enable high performance in perovskite solar cells, but controlling the hole extraction efficiency is challenging. Tianyu Li et al. address this by designing molecules that adopt a quasi-random orientation on the substrate.

records.title: The team behind the publishing process
records.description: Every paper we publish is shaped by a dedicated team of production, art, copy, and editorial staff who guide it from submission to publication. This Q&A series highlights their behind-the-scenes work.

records.description: Every paper we publish is shaped by a dedicated team of production, art, copy, and editorial staff who guide it from submission to publication. This Q&A series highlights their behind-the-scenes work. Here, we speak with Kevin Sheridan, Subeditor at the journal, about his responsibilities and how they fit into the broader editorial workflow.

records.description: Every paper we publish is shaped by a dedicated team of production, art, copy, and editorial staff who guide it from submission to publication. This Q&A series highlights their behind-the-scenes work — here we speak with Robert Parker, Production Editor at the journal, about his responsibilities and how they fit into the broader editorial workflow.

records.description: Every paper we publish is shaped by a dedicated team of production, art, copy, and editorial staff who guide it from submission to publication. This Q&A series highlights their behind-the-scenes work — here we speak with Katilyn Brown, Editorial Assistant at the journal, about her responsibilities and how they fit into the broader editorial workflow.
