records.description: Every paper we publish is shaped by a dedicated team of production, art, copy, and editorial staff who guide it from submission to publication. This Q&A series highlights their behind-the-scenes work — here we speak with Thomas Phillips, Art Editor at the journal, about his responsibilities and how they fit into the broader editorial workflow.

records.title: Author Correction: Photoswitchable isomers to improve grain boundary resilience and perovskite solar cells stability under light cycling
Contact-triggered molecular interactions enable structural refinement of perovskite layers in solar cells
records.description: Solution processing of 2D/3D perovskite structures for solar cells offers limited control over layer formation. Lee et al. propose a dry approach, bringing the 2D and 3D perovskite layers into physical contact, to enhance the quality of the perovskite film.

records.title: A molecularly engineered electron-selective self-assembled monolayer enhances quasi-Fermi level splitting in inverted perovskite solar cells
records.description: Voltage losses at the perovskite/C 60 interface limit the efficiency of perovskite solar cells. Mubai Li et al. design an electron-selective charge-transport self-assembled monolayer that balances electron extraction and the interfacial charge-carrier density.

records.title: Decoupling cation segregation and volatile loss in formamidinium–caesium metal halide perovskite solar cells under high-temperature operating conditions
records.description: The stability of perovskite photovoltaics under thermal and light stress remains poorly understood. Wang et al. identify cation segregation and volatilization of formamidinium iodide as the primary degradation pathways at different temperatures.

records.title: Fusion power experience rates are overestimated
records.description: The cost reductions projected for fusion power technologies are overly optimistic. An analysis of technology characteristics implies likely experience rates of 2–8% for fusion power plants, rather than the currently assumed 8–20%.

records.title: Amorphous self-assembled multilayers for perovskite solar cells with improved reverse bias stability
records.description: The morphology of hole-selective contacts is key to the stability of perovskite solar cells. Feng et al. use self-assembled molecules with extended conjugation and hydroxyl groups to form dense, amorphous films that suppress degradation induced by ion migration.

records.title: Alkali-metal-mediated control of phase segregation for flexible kesterite solar cells and modules with improved efficiency
records.description: The incorporation of alkali metals in kesterite solar cells enables high efficiency but is challenging to control. Xu et al. show that combining Na and Li ions yields optimal phase formation, enabling efficient solar cells and modules.

records.title: Exploiting the insulator–metal transition of VO 2 in photocatalytic methane conversion
records.description: Photocatalysts for methane conversion can suffer from inefficient charge carrier diffusion, limiting their effectiveness. Here the authors exploit the insulator–metal transition in VO 2 to create an electronic phase junction, enhancing the non-oxidative conversion of methane into hydrogen, ethane and propane, with peak efficiency at the transition’s critical temperature.

records.title: Additive-assisted perovskite crystallization on industrial TOPCon silicon for tandem solar cells with improved efficiency
records.description: Crystallizing the perovskite layer on thin tunnel oxide passivated contact silicon cells is challenging due to rapid heat transfer. Zhou et al. address this issue using a 2-mercaptobenzothiazole additive, achieving a tandem cell efficiency of 32.76%.

records.title: Irreversible organic cations chemistry limits organic–inorganic halide perovskite stability under illumination or bias
records.description: Oxidation and reduction reactions undermine the stability of perovskite solar cells under illumination and bias. In this Perspective, Ren et al. examine the impact of irreversible reactions involving organic cations, identify key knowledge gaps, and outline strategies for mitigation.

records.title: Understanding UK public preferences and attitudes to a decarbonized heating system
records.description: Substantial heterogeneity is evident in stances towards the development of aquifer thermal energy storage (ATES) systems in the UK. An assessment of individual preferences reveals substantial valuations of specific ATES characteristics that are nevertheless modified by latent attitudes regarding systemic and local benefits, safety concerns, information provision, and policy support.

records.title: Author Correction: Heterogeneity in public attitudes and preferences for the deployment of aquifer thermal energy storage
Bifacial tunnel oxide passivating contacts for silicon and perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells with improved efficiency
records.description: Interfacial charge recombination losses limit solar cell efficiency. Gao et al. mitigate these losses through front and rear-contact engineering, achieving efficiencies of 26.34% and 32.73% in tunnel oxide passivating contact single-junction and tandem solar cells.

records.title: Reversible solutions
records.description: Improved technologies are required to curb the substantial greenhouse gas emissions associated with heating and cooling. Researchers have now revisited endothermic cooling to design a sustainable, reversible sorption-driven dissolution refrigeration cycle, which holds broad potential for cooling, heating, and thermal storage applications.

records.title: Sorption-driven dissolution refrigeration cycle with thermal storage
records.description: New technologies are needed to reduce the large greenhouse gas footprint of heating and cooling. Wu et al. propose a reversible sorption-driven dissolution refrigeration cycle with promise for cooling, heating and thermal energy storage.

records.title: Challenges, technological pathways and trade-offs of perovskite solar modules for long-term operation
records.description: The operational stability of perovskite solar modules under real-world conditions remains a critical challenge. In this Review, Luigi A. Castriotta et al. analyse the degradation pathways and discuss how accelerated tests can predict outdoor performance.

records.title: Solvent-enabled fast kinetics
records.description: Electrolyte solvents in sodium-ion batteries have long been regarded as passive ion-transport media, while sluggish Na + diffusion in layered cathodes limits kinetics. Now, researchers show that reversible solvent intercalation actively enhances Na + transport, enabling fast kinetics with preserved redox chemistry and cycling stability.

records.title: Letting ions slide
records.description: Salinity gradients can be converted into electrical energy via charge-selective membranes, yet controlling the solid–liquid interfacial properties at the nanometre scale remains a key challenge. Now, highly charged nanopores coated with a lipid bilayer are shown to enable hydration lubrication, enhancing ion transport, selectivity and osmotic power generation.

records.title: Heterogeneity in public attitudes and preferences for the deployment of aquifer thermal energy storage
records.description: Survey and discrete choice experiment data reveal substantial heterogeneity in the UK public’s stance towards aquifer thermal energy storage deployment and in preferences for deployment characteristics that vary with latent attitudes.

records.title: Solvent intercalation in layered cathodes for ultrafast sodium-ion batteries
records.description: Rechargeable sodium-ion batteries are limited by slow ion movement in cathodes. Here the authors show that introducing solvent molecules into layered cathodes improves ion transport and reaction kinetics, enabling fast-charging batteries with stable long-term performance.

records.title: Mapping innovation priorities for rapid green power growth towards 2030
records.description: Experts from 13 countries gathered in Yancheng, China to share recent research and technological and operational progress in renewable energy integration, and to identify urgent solutions in some key areas needed to accelerate the global energy transition.

records.title: Uniform pore structure enables negligible degradation in undoped and uncoated Ni-rich cathodes
records.description: Nickel-rich layered oxide cathodes suffer from chemomechanical degradation, and current mitigation methods require complex syntheses. Here the researchers show that simple control of LiOH melting produces uniform microstructures that stabilize the cathodes without doping or coatings.

records.title: Emerging roles of cations in electrocatalytic reduction of CO 2 and CO
records.description: Cations play a crucial role in electrocatalytic reduction of CO 2 and CO to fuels and chemicals, influencing activity and selectivity. This Review explores their effects as indirect mediators, energetic modulators and electron-transfer participants, highlighting key mechanistic insights and knowledge gaps.

records.title: Longer lifetimes through quantum effects
records.description: The effectiveness of solar-driven water splitting is constrained by inefficient separation of photogenerated charge carriers and their rapid recombination. Researchers now show that multilayered structures that exhibit quantum effects by confining electrons in thin layers can optimize charge carrier dynamics, resulting in photocatalysts with remarkable efficiency.

records.title: Balancing adsorption
The solid–gas interphase
Ambient air operation
Gender diversity for enhanced resilience
Cross‑field insights
records.description: Energy technologies may differ in underlying operation and purpose, but insights from one can often inform progress in another.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Ethylene production via photocatalytic dehydrogenation of ethane using LaMn 1− x Cu x O 3
Photoswitchable isomers to improve grain boundary resilience and perovskite solar cells stability under light cycling
records.description: The operational stability of perovskite solar cells remains a challenge. Zhang et al. incorporate photoswitchable isomers at grain boundaries to improve their resilience and the stability of the solar cells under light cycling and ultraviolet exposure.

records.title: Regulating grain growth via Li 2 SnS 3 interphase in kesterite solar cells with certified efficiencies exceeding 15%
records.description: Selenization is a key step in kesterite solar cell fabrication, but controlling ion migration during this process is challenging. Cui et al. address this issue by introducing a Li 2 SnS 3 interphase, achieving a certified power conversion efficiency of 15.0%.

records.title: Dual-side electrical refinement enables efficient industrial tunnel oxide passivating contact silicon solar cells
records.description: Tunnel oxide passivating contact silicon solar cells are a promising next-generation photovoltaic technology. Yang et al. engineer the front and back contact, further increasing the power conversion efficiency to 26.66%.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Self-assembled molecules with hydrogen-bond networks enable efficient all-perovskite tandem solar cells
Redefining dry electrode architecture
records.description: The pursuit of high-energy-density batteries is often limited by slurry-based processing, because thicker electrodes suffer from reaction heterogeneity. Now, by molecularly engineering the carbon–binder network, a dry electrode architecture is introduced that enables stable high-voltage operation without the need to redesign active materials or the electrolyte.

records.title: Chemical factors controlling the behaviour of oxide cathodes in batteries
records.description: Oxide cathodes underpin both Li- and Na-ion batteries, but their performance is often interpreted empirically. This Perspective shows how intrinsic chemical factors govern their behaviour and offers guidance for designing more stable, higher-energy cathodes.

records.title: Dry electrode architecture design to push energy density limits at the cell level
records.description: Conventional slurry electrodes limit high-energy lithium batteries. This work shows that dry-processed electrodes with molecularly coupled carbon–binder networks enable high mass and active material loading, supporting stable high-voltage operation and enhancing battery energy density.

records.title: Knowledge interdependencies between lithium- and sodium-ion battery chemistries
records.description: How knowledge is shared across different battery chemistries is important to industrial strategy and techno-economic forecasting but remains poorly understood. Here the authors perform large language model-based patent analysis of over 15,000 families and show sustained knowledge flows between and within lithium-ion and sodium-ion batteries, indicating interdependence across chemistries.

records.title: A cation-functionalized layer for ethylene electrosynthesis via CO reduction paired with H 2 oxidation in a pure-water-fed solid-state electrolyser
records.description: Electroreduction of CO is an emerging route to produce multicarbon molecules, but achieving this efficiently in solid-state devices is challenging. Here the authors develop a cation-functionalized layer using polyacrylate in a solid-state electrolyser that produces ethylene stably and efficiently from syngas.

records.title: Energy packed tightly
records.description: Sodium-ion batteries face a volumetric disadvantage because dense anodes often lose electrical connectivity during cycling. A dense alloy anode is now designed to maintain connectivity, enabling ampere-hour-class pouch cells with higher volumetric energy density and longer cycle life.

records.title: Charge and slip-length optimization in lipid-bilayer-coated nanofluidics for enhanced osmotic energy harvesting
records.description: Salinity gradients can be converted into electrical energy via charge-selective membranes. Here the authors report a nanofluidic system based on stalactite nanopore membranes functionalized with charged lipid bilayers for osmotic energy harvesting with enhanced ion transport and charge separation efficiency.

records.title: Durable alloy anode for Na-ion batteries with high volumetric energy density
records.description: Alloy anodes can boost the energy density of Na-ion batteries but suffer from instability, and current strategies trade off performance and scalability. Here the authors develop a high-loading Sn anode reinforced with single-walled carbon nanotube networks, achieving high capacity and long-term cycling performance.

records.title: Early market opportunity for long-duration energy storage
records.description: Multi-day, long-duration energy storage (LDES) is essential for decarbonizing the power grid, yet grid-scale deployment of LDES faces steep cost, scale and risk barriers. Behind-the-meter backup power applications for large commercial and medical facilities offer an early market; targeting this could overcome all three barriers and accelerate the adoption of LDES.

records.title: Electrified reversible surface mineralization of CO 2 for direct air capture
records.description: Electrified CO 2 capture from air could lead to net-negative emissions, yet current methods face high energy costs and sensitivity to oxygen. Here the authors introduce an electrochemical approach using MnO 2 as a stable, redox-active sorbent, achieving CO 2 capture with promising energy consumption and minimal oxygen sensitivity.

records.title: Electrolyte design curbs side reactions
records.description: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries offer strong potential for high-energy grid storage but rely on acidic conditions that cause severe zinc corrosion. Now, a hybrid eutectic aqueous–organic electrolyte is reported that suppresses side reactions and enables highly reversible, durable Zn‖MnO 2 cycling without added acid.

records.title: Suppressing intermediate crystallization for flexible tandem solar cells
records.description: A crystallization strategy enables the successful deposition, through blade-coating under ambient conditions, of phase-pure, wide-bandgap perovskite films with a homogeneous halide distribution. Using this approach, a monolithic perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 tandem solar cell achieved a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% and exhibited high operational stability.

records.title: Translating insights from progress in photovoltaics to accelerate industrial-scale CO 2 electroreduction
records.description: Electrochemical CO 2 conversion holds promise for producing fuels and chemicals, yet faces hurdles in scaling to industrial levels. In this Perspective, drawing lessons from photovoltaics, the authors discuss measures to help transition the technology from the laboratory to large-scale deployment.

records.title: Buried 2D/3D heterojunction in n–i–p perovskite solar cells through solid-state ligand-exchange reaction
records.description: Two-dimensional perovskite phases at the bottom interfaces of solar cells improve performance, but their formation is challenging. To address this, Zhao et al. graft the 2D perovskite-phase precursor onto a functionalized SnO 2 electrode substrate.

records.title: Addressing context-specific energy modelling risks and dynamics in low- and middle-income countries
records.description: Low- and middle-income countries face unique challenges when it comes to balancing growing energy needs with broader, long-term development needs. This Perspective argues for innovative, context-specific modelling practices to support these goals.

records.title: Self-assembled molecules with hydrogen-bond networks enable efficient all-perovskite tandem solar cells
records.description: Self-assembled monolayers are efficient hole-selective contacts but suffer from aggregation and adhesion issues. To address these, Wang et al. introduce a dimeric molecular design that forms a hydrogen-bond network, enabling 28.4% certified efficiency in all-perovskite tandem solar cells.

records.title: Aligning electrons for speed
records.description: The application of Li-metal batteries is limited by parasitic interfacial reactions that slow charge transfer at the anode. A tailored electrolyte that forms a planar Li⁺–solvent complex with aligned electron channels overcomes this barrier, enabling fast reduction kinetics under demanding conditions.

records.title: Mechanistic understanding of interphase-driven ageing in silicon anodes
records.description: Silicon anodes promise much higher battery capacity but are limited by poor storage life. This work identifies key ageing mechanisms and suggests ways to improve long-term stability.

records.title: Excitonic quantum superlattices for efficient photocatalytic water splitting
records.description: Splitting water using sunlight is a promising route to green hydrogen, yet inefficient charge carrier utilization in photocatalysts limits their solar-to-hydrogen efficiency. Here the authors introduce excitonic quantum superlattices to prolong exciton lifetimes and optimize charge steering, achieving a solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of 3% under ambient conditions.

records.title: Crystallization suppression of mixed-halide intermediates for perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 tandem solar cells with improved efficiency
records.description: The efficiency of perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 tandem solar cells is limited by halide segregation in the perovskite layer. Zhang et al. use 2-pyrrolidinone to slow the crystallization of halide intermediates, ensuring a homogeneous distribution and achieving a power conversion efficiency of 27.3%.

records.title: Author Correction: Mapping Europe’s rooftop photovoltaic potential with a building-level database
Justice as a measure of energy transition success
records.description: Energy justice has shifted from the margins to become a central aspect of energy transitions research, argues Destenie Nock.

records.title: The integration imperative in electricity grid transition
records.description: As the grid adapts to a changing energy landscape, its traditional role must evolve to balance cost, reliability, and emerging system priorities through fresh thinking in technology, markets, and institutional design, says Mark O’Malley.

records.title: Nuclear reactors are too expensive and slow to build
records.description: Nuclear power continues to pose economic and practical barriers to expanded deployment, argues M. V. Ramana.

records.title: Urban energy transformation through integrated systems
records.description: As digital tools and sector coupling enable coordinated infrastructure and empower stakeholders, integrated energy systems are driving the transition to low-carbon urban energy, writes Jinyue Yan.

records.title: Unforeseen triumphs in batteries and the road ahead
records.description: Battery technology has advanced at extraordinary speed over the past decade, yet meeting the world’s accelerating electrification needs will require both continued evolution of lithium-ion systems and further progress in next-generation chemistries, writes Peter Bruce.

records.title: Embracing change in electrocatalysis
records.description: Electrocatalytic conversion of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) — an emerging approach using electricity to produce useful molecules — has advanced enormously over the past ten years. However, to progress further, we must move away from the traditional static description of catalytic surfaces, argues Beatriz Roldan Cuenya.

records.title: Sustainable cooling will require novel refrigerants and technologies
records.description: To curb greenhouse gas emissions from conventional vapour compression cooling technologies, it is necessary to develop refrigerants with low global warming potential and solid-state caloric cooling devices, argues Ichiro Takeuchi.

records.title: Advances in the performance and adoption of solar photovoltaics
records.description: Martin Green discusses how, over the past decade — and continuing today — we have witnessed a rapid increase in solar photovoltaic installations, a sharp decline in costs, and swift transitions in the dominant market technologies.

records.title: Access to finance will determine who can participate in the electrification race
records.description: Financial support and research must concentrate on levelling the playing field to ensure emerging and developing economies will benefit from electrification, argues Florian Egli.

records.title: Collaboration can secure carbon capture’s future
records.description: After years of technical advances and billions in public funding, carbon capture’s promise now depends on creative alliances — between incumbents and innovators, across borders and sectors — to safeguard past investments and deliver lasting climate impact, writes Jennifer Wilcox.

records.title: Advancing wind energy through better understanding of the atmosphere
records.description: Wind variability, turbine wake effects, and extreme events are not just challenges but opportunities to deepen our understanding of the atmosphere and enhance the resilience of wind energy systems, argues Julie Lundquist.

records.title: Marking ten years of Nature Energy
records.description: This issue marks ten years of Nature Energy , offering a moment to reflect on a decade of energy research and to look ahead at what comes next.

records.title: The highs and lows of hydrogen
records.description: The hydrogen ecosystem has developed substantially over the past decade, yet investment volatility and other challenges will require a reinvigorated and cohesive effort to enable success, writes Sunita Satyapal.

records.title: An evolving research agenda for the transition to electrified transport
records.description: Transport electrification is reshaping energy and mobility systems while posing infrastructure, supply chain, and societal challenges that demand bold, interconnected research, argues Patrick Plötz.

records.title: Levers to address energy insecurity in the United States
records.description: A wide range of policies and actions can be used to address energy insecurity, and there are many actors and institutions to carry them out. This Perspective provides an overview of the many levers, or opportunities, that electricity sector actors have to reduce energy insecurity and affordability in the United States.

records.title: Aqueous eutectic electrolytes suppress oxygen and hydrogen evolution for long-life Zn||MnO 2 dual-electrode-free batteries
records.description: Eutectic aqueous–organic electrolytes enable highly reversible zinc–manganese batteries without acid addition. By regulating the water-bonding network, beneficial manganese oxide phases are deposited and stripped while gas formation is suppressed, achieving ultraextended cycling.

records.title: Molecularly aligned electron channels for ultrafast-charging practical lithium-metal batteries
records.description: Sluggish interfacial charge transfer in Li-metal batteries limits ultrafast charging and causes side reactions. The authors design solvent molecules to enhance Li⁺ coordination, improving the charge-transfer kinetics and enabling stable high-rate cycling of Li-metal cells.

records.title: Managing the geopolitics of Europe’s fossil-fuel exit
records.description: As Europe gradually phases out its fossil-fuel imports, some producer economies face rising risks. With careful management, the European Union can turn this shift into an opportunity to advance both climate leadership and geopolitical stability.

records.title: Atomistic origins of anharmonic lattice dynamics and thermal expansion in perovskite photovoltaics
records.description: Metal halide perovskites exhibit anharmonic lattice vibrations, which lead to high rates of thermal expansion in solar cells. In this Review, Julian A. Steele links the atomistic origins of these effects to the macroscopic thermo-mechanical properties of the materials and devices.

records.title: Harnessing interfacial solvation structure for next-generation secondary batteries
records.description: Ion–solvent interactions at battery interfaces share parallels with solvation effects in catalysis. This analysis examines how interfacial solvation structures influence interphase formation and charge transfer, offering insights into electrochemical behaviour under complex conditions.

records.title: Lessons from copper indium gallium sulfo-selenide solar cells for progressing perovskite photovoltaics
records.description: Perovskite photovoltaics could benefit from insights gained through the longer history of other photovoltaic technologies. In this Perspective, Bermudez and colleagues examine how lessons from the successes and failures of copper indium gallium selenide solar cells can guide future progress.

records.title: Behavioural choices shape US indoor temperatures more than technology
records.description: Households that manually manage thermostats keep homes warmer in winter and cooler in summer than those using automated smart thermostat features, leading to increased energy use and costs. Expanding equitable access to smart thermostats and supporting behavioural engagement could improve indoor thermal comfort, reduce energy costs, and narrow disparities in thermal safety.

records.title: The role of thermostats and human behaviour in residential temperature settings in the USA
records.description: Smart thermostats and programmed temperature settings support more efficient heating and cooling. New research finds that renters, low-income and Black households are less likely to have this technology in the USA.

records.title: Regulation of hydrothermal kinetics unlocks record efficiency in Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cells
records.description: Regulating hydrothermal reaction kinetics using sodium sulfide achieves a flattened valence band maximum across the Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 film, lifting the potential barrier for hole transport while suppressing deep-level defect formation and reducing trap centres. This strategy enables Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cells to reach a certified record efficiency of 10.7%.

records.title: Regulation of hydrothermal reaction kinetics with sodium sulfide for certified 10.7% efficiency Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cells
records.description: Controlling the hydrothermal reaction kinetics during the fabrication of Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cells is challenging. Chen Qian et al. show that sodium sulfide buffers the pH and allows a controlled release of Se, enabling a certified efficiency of 10.7%.

records.title: Co-crystal engineering unlocks high-stability perovskite solar modules
records.description: Instability hinders the commercialization of perovskite solar cells. Now, a co-crystal engineering strategy is developed to create a protective two-dimensional perovskite layer on top of a three-dimensional perovskite layer. This approach increases the stability and efficiency of perovskite solar modules, surpassing current photovoltaic standards, in a step towards industrial manufacturing.

records.title: Battery-electric passenger vehicles will be cost-effective across Africa well before 2040
records.description: Decarbonizing road transport is critical, but the costs and emissions of low-carbon vehicles in Africa remain uncertain. The authors show that battery electric vehicles with solar off-grid systems can cost effectively reduce life-cycle emissions well before 2040.

records.title: Mapping Europe’s rooftop photovoltaic potential with a building-level database
records.description: This resource presents an open per-building dataset of rooftop solar photovoltaics potential for the European Union. The results show that potential capacity could cover approximately 40% of electricity demand in a 100% renewable scenario for 2050.

records.title: Formation pathway of high-efficiency kesterite solar cells fabricated through molecular ink chemistry
records.description: Photovoltaics based on kesterite materials have now achieved 15% efficiency after remaining at lower levels for years. In this Review, Jimenez-Arguijo et al. explore the critical roles of precursor chemistry and the formation pathway in enabling performance improvements in these complex multinary semiconductors.

records.title: A just energy transition requires just-shoring critical materials
Selenium hits double digits
records.description: Of the many families of solar absorber materials known, only a handful have been shown to convert sunlight into electricity with power conversion efficiencies above 10%. Now, researchers have pushed selenium photovoltaics past this efficiency threshold by implementing a series of improvements to the material processing and device design.

records.title: Illumination-assisted annealing enables selenium solar cells with open-circuit voltage over 1 V and efficiency exceeding 10%
records.description: The efficiency of selenium photovoltaics is hindered by the poor crystallization of the Se film. Wen, Li, Lu and colleagues use light to initiate Se crystallization, suppressing dewetting and enabling the formation of a continuous film, which achieves a certified efficiency of 10.3%.

records.title: Fuel poverty risk at the end of life needs urgent attention
records.description: Proactive policy and economic support are needed to reduce fuel poverty risk at the end of life, argues Elaine Robinson.

records.title: Amorphous grain boundary engineering for scalable flexible perovskite photovoltaics with improved stability
records.description: The mechanical reliability and scalability of flexible perovskite solar cells remain challenging. Mingzhu He et al. design β-cyclodextrin derivatives to reinforce grain boundaries, enhancing both the efficiency and stability of cells and modules.

records.title: Negative pricing increases electricity use but challenges grid stability
records.description: When electricity supply exceeds demand, consumers can be paid to use electricity through negative pricing. Simulations based on national surveys indicate that such pricing could double electricity loads in many US counties. However, market policies and grids must be carefully designed to avoid destabilizing the power grid with demand surges.

records.title: Approaching the theoretical density limit of ultrahigh-nickel cathodes via cation-disorder-free 10-μm single-crystalline particles
records.description: Single-crystalline layered oxides can reduce capacity decay in nickel-rich cathodes, but controlling both the particle size and cation disorder is challenging. This work reports cation-disorder-free ~10-μm single-crystalline cathodes that deliver high volumetric capacity and cycle stability as well as improved safety.
